articles.title: PwC US Launches Certification Program for Employees to Develop Critical Thinking Skills
articles.summary: The program aims to equip over 85,000 employees in PwC's US and Mexico offices with essential skills as artificial intelligence takes over routine tasks.
articles.content: PwC US is launching a certification program for its employees to develop critical thinking and judgment skills as artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly takes over routine tasks. The program will be open to over 85,000 workers in PwC's US and Mexico offices, including those in Acceleration Centers that support client work and business operations. According to Yolanda Seals-Coffield, chief people and inclusion officer at PwC US, the initiative is designed to equip employees with essential skills for their roles. The certification program is set to begin in December, as part of a broader effort by the company to adapt its workforce to the changing landscape brought about by AI. This technology has already started to automate tasks such as research, writing, and analysis that were previously carried out manually. As AI assumes these foundational responsibilities, employees may no longer have opportunities to develop their critical thinking and judgment skills through repetitive tasks. PwC has identified a set of essential human skills that will become increasingly valuable as AI assumes more responsibilities in the workplace. These skills include empathy and adaptability, among others, which are seen as key differentiators for employees. The company's certification program focuses on critical thinking and judgment, two skills that PwC considers crucial for success in an AI-driven work environment. In this context, critical thinking encompasses a range of abilities, including evaluating information, establishing context, challenging assumptions, refining analysis, and communicating recommendations. To help employees develop these essential skills, the company is working with professors and veteran staff to create classes that will enable participants to sharpen their thinking abilities. The program aims to identify each individual's natural strengths and areas where they may need additional focus. The certification process involves an initial assessment to determine a person's thinking style and how it influences their judgment. This evaluation considers whether the individual is inclined to question assumptions, reflect on information, or adopt a more practical approach. The personalized AI coach will play a crucial role in helping employees apply their critical thinking skills learned through simulations to their daily tasks. This might involve practicing difficult conversations or preparing for client meetings by uploading proposals and having the coach review them. The coach can also help identify which team member is best suited for each task, ensuring that workloads are distributed effectively. The program's curriculum will be tailored to employees' seniority levels, with content customized to meet their specific needs. This approach reflects PwC's focus on equipping staff with the skills necessary for a rapidly changing job market, where AI is increasingly prevalent. Critical thinking and judgment are seen as complementary to other key areas of instruction, including responsible use of AI and professional skepticism. Development leaders will evaluate employees' proficiency in applying critical thinking skills through their performance reviews, which will take place throughout the certification process. The program's rollout is planned in stages, allowing staff ample time to absorb and apply the lessons learned before being assessed on their progress. This gradual approach aims to ensure that employees have sufficient opportunities to develop their skills. The goal of the certification program is for participants to complete it by June 2027, with the idea being to equip them with repeatable skills rather than simply preparing them for a traditional pass/fail exam. By doing so, PwC hopes to create an environment where staff can be assessed and evaluated based on their demonstrated ability to apply critical thinking in real-world scenarios. The certification program is part of PwC's broader efforts to adapt its hiring practices in response to changing industry demands. The company has shifted its focus towards recruiting engineers and technologists across all its businesses, rather than just its traditional advisory sector. This shift is reflected in the types of roles available within the firm, with engineers now working not only in the advisory business but also in tax and assurance divisions. PwC continues to actively recruit on college campuses and make offers to a significant proportion of its summer interns, suggesting that the company remains committed to attracting top talent. The certification program aims to ensure that employees possess both AI-driven skills and human proficiencies throughout their careers. By continually assessing staff against these dual criteria, PwC seeks to create a robust and adaptable workforce capable of navigating an increasingly complex professional landscape. With six ranked-versus-ranked matchups in Week 10, the stakes were high and the consequences of defeat severe. The results of these high-stakes games have led to significant changes in the rankings. One team that benefited greatly from its Week 10 performance was Notre Dame, which secured a crucial victory over Miami. The Fighting Irish had been sent a clear message by the College Football Playoff Committee: beat Miami and avoid another disappointing postseason absence. They responded with a season-saving 31-24 win. Notre Dame's quarterback CJ Carr played a pivotal role in the team's success, displaying pinpoint accuracy throughout the game. He consistently found open receivers and exploited weaknesses in the Miami secondary, while also limiting damage to his own defense. The Irish's defensive unit was equally impressive, shutting down two potential game-winning drives by the Hurricanes. The implications of Notre Dame's victory are far-reaching, with the team now firmly positioned for a strong finish to the season. With this win under its belt, the Fighting Irish will look to build momentum and secure a coveted spot in the College Football Playoff. The Georgia Bulldogs are making a strong case for being the top team in college football after their dominating performance against Ole Miss. Their 5-TD quarterback Gunner Stockton silenced critics who had questioned his abilities earlier in the season. The team's overall performance was impressive, with both lines of scrimmage thoroughly dominated by the Bulldogs. The Crimson Tide, ranked #5 in the first CFP rankings, also made a statement on the field with their win over LSU. After facing questions about their ranking, they proved their worth with a 31-13 victory that showcased their capabilities. The win was particularly notable given the team's struggles earlier in the season. With several key games remaining on their schedule, including a matchup against Texas A&M, the team will have opportunities to prove themselves further. Wake Forest's chances of making the College Football Playoff (CFP) have improved significantly after a crucial weekend for the Demon Deacons. The key factor was that several teams ranked above Wake Forest suffered losses, creating an opportunity for the team to move up the list. According to initial CFP committee rankings, Wake Forest needed some help to make the 12-team playoff this season, and they received it on Saturday when five teams ranked seven spots or less ahead of them lost. With these setbacks, Wake Forest will now have a stronger case to secure a spot in the CFP, especially with several key games remaining on their schedule. articles.title: Breakthrough Discovery Explains Origin of Anna's Hummingbird's Magenta Feathers
articles.summary: A team led by Sangyeop Kim has identified a hidden layer inside the feathers of male Anna's hummingbirds that produces the blue reflection necessary for their distinctive magenta color.
articles.content: A team of scientists has made a breakthrough discovery about the brilliant magenta feathers found on the head and throat of male Anna's hummingbirds. These vibrant colors have long been a subject of fascination, but their origin has remained somewhat of an optical puzzle. Magenta is not a color that can be produced by a single wavelength of light, which means that the feathers must reflect a combination of different wavelengths to achieve this distinctive hue. While the strong red reflection in these feathers was already understood, scientists struggled to explain the weaker blue component. This has been a long-standing mystery in the field of ornithology. A team led by Sangyeop Kim from Yonsei University has now identified a previously overlooked region inside the feathers that plays a crucial role in producing the blue reflection. According to their research, this hidden layer works together with material near the surface of the feather to create the distinctive magenta color. The scientists tested their theory by gradually eroding the surface of the feather, which resulted in a significant decrease in the blue reflection. As the blue component faded, the feathers' appearance changed from magenta to orange, providing visual evidence for the team's explanation. This breakthrough builds on previous research that revealed the internal architecture of these feathers is responsible for their shimmering appearance. A 2018 study had already shown how stacked structures inside the feathers produce both the strong red and weaker blue reflections, but it was unable to fully reproduce the blue component. The research delved deeper into the structures within the feathers of Anna's hummingbird to understand their role in producing the bird's vibrant plumage. Specifically, it focused on the stacks of melanosomes and air cavities found inside barbules, which are tiny branches extending from a feather's main stem. Each stack consists of flattened melanosomes containing melanin pigment, as well as air cavities embedded within a matrix of protein. The interaction between light waves reflected from the boundaries between these different materials contributes to the final color we see. This phenomenon is influenced by the thickness and arrangement of the layers. The study's findings revealed that earlier descriptions of the melanosomes' size and distribution were incomplete. Electron microscopy images showed a more nuanced picture, with a gradual transition from smaller structures near the surface to larger ones deeper inside. A significant portion of this difference was due to variations in the size of air pockets within the melanosomes. Computer simulations demonstrated how including the intermediate layers affected the color produced by the feather's structure. When these layers were omitted or treated as uniformly thick, a strong red reflection resulted but without a distinct blue peak. However, when the intermediate layers were included, the blue peak became visible, highlighting their crucial role in producing the bird's magenta feathers. The researchers used oxygen plasma etching to gradually remove surface material from real hummingbird feathers and observe how their color changed over time. After 60 seconds of treatment, the outer protein covering was almost completely gone, revealing reddish-orange barbules underneath. By this stage, the color had already begun to shift away from its original appearance. Further erosion revealed air cavities in the upper melanosomes after another 60 seconds. Measurements showed that as the surface material continued to erode, the blue reflection weakened and eventually disappeared. At the same time, the dominant red reflection shifted towards shorter wavelengths, giving it an orange hue. This transformation supported the researchers' models of how the middle and surface regions work together to produce color. The study raises questions about how the different-sized structures within a feather develop as it grows. Researchers also do not yet know whether other hummingbird species have the same arrangement in their feathers. Tiny differences in buried air pockets are crucial to determining whether the reflected light from the feather appears orange or produces a vibrant flash of magenta. This unique structure could potentially inspire the development of materials with adjustable colors for use in displays or security markings. The discovery of a hidden middle layer in Anna's hummingbird feathers has shed new light on the bird's brilliant magenta coloration. This unique structure, which is made up of tiny, intricately arranged melanin granules, plays a crucial role in producing the bird's distinctive plumage. This middle layer acts as a "photonic mechanism" that amplifies and modifies the colors produced by the outer layers of the feather, resulting in the vibrant magenta hue. The researchers' findings suggest that this multi-periodic structure could potentially be replicated to create materials with adjustable colors for use in displays or security markings. This breakthrough has significant implications for our understanding of color production in nature and its potential applications in technology. His partner, Michèle Lamy, is attending RuPaul's Drag Race as a guest judge, and Owens' schedule allowed for a brief window of time to speak with our reporter. The new Adidas collection is the culmination of Owens' long history in fashion, which spans nearly three decades. He refers to those who work with him or are loyal fans of his brand as part of his "family, suggesting a strong sense of loyalty and connection to his community. Rick Owens has reunited with Adidas to create a new line of shoes, leveraging their innovative springblade technology. This cutting-edge feature consists of futuristic blades at the sole of the shoe, which gives the footwear an unmistakable avant-garde look. The collaboration between Owens and Adidas is not just about creating a new product but also about unifying his team behind a shared brand identity. As Owens himself put it, getting his team to switch from other branded sneakers to their own was a key motivation for this partnership. By using Adidas' technology, Owens aimed to create runners that would meet the high standards of both brands. The shoes were first showcased during Owens' spring 2027 runway show in June, where they made a dramatic impression alongside his ready-to-wear designs. The silhouette of these shoes is reminiscent of Brutalist architecture, with clean lines and minimalist aesthetic. One notable feature is the use of fabric that folds over the foot to create a deflated bag-like shape. The Adidas collaboration extends beyond footwear to encompass various apparel items such as hooded capes, tracksuit pants in different silhouettes, sleeveless tunics, jackets, and bodysuits. These pieces incorporate elements from Owens' previous collections, including his Taco series, which features a folded piece of fabric over the foot. The show's concept of inflated garments combines elements from various sources, including blow-up Halloween costumes and the iconic scene from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory where Violet Beauregarde turns into a blueberry. This unique approach was driven by Rick Owens' desire to create an impactful runway show without generating excessive waste. Owens revealed that he considers sustainability when planning his shows, aiming to avoid building elaborate sets that are ultimately destroyed after the event. The use of inflated garments as a design element aligns with this goal, providing a lightweight and easily transportable solution. This approach also allows Owens to blend innovative technology with more traditional and naive methods. Inflated garments have been used in various contexts for decades, particularly by Japanese workers who have incorporated them into their designs. Adidas adopted this concept around 20 years ago, and now Rick Owens is building upon it as part of his collaboration with the brand. The inflated pieces will not only be showcased on the runway but also produced for purchase. Owens' intention behind creating a more accessible and feasible show is to make his designs feel less like an impossible dream". He draws inspiration from earlier runway shows, where elaborate sets were often used as a spectacle before being discarded. By incorporating inflated garments into his design, Owens aims to create a sense of wonder without the environmental cost. Rick Owens' design philosophy emphasizes accessibility and functionality, a departure from what he perceives as the superficiality of collaborations in the fashion world. To him, collaborations often feel like setting aside fine china for special occasions, implying that they are not part of everyday life. He wants to create clothing that people can wear regularly, not just for show or on rare occasions. The Adidas collaboration is an exception because it gives Owens complete creative freedom, allowing him to produce designs that genuinely reflect his vision rather than conforming to commercial expectations. Rick Owens' approach to fashion is deeply rooted in functionality and comfort. His go-to gym outfit consists of simple, practical pieces such as baggy shorts and thin T-shirts, which allow him to move freely without restricting his movements. When traveling, Owens often favors hotel slippers over sneakers due to space constraints in his carry-on luggage. He has expressed a desire to collaborate with Adidas on creating a comfortable workout shoe that meets his needs for both performance and practicality, hinting at the possibility of future designs with the brand. articles.title: Nacon's Revolution 5 Unlimited controller is an officially licensed PlayStation 5 gamepad that works with PCs
articles.summary: The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited controller offers a high level of customization with features like customizable shortcut buttons and control profiles, as well as interchangeable joystick heads.
articles.content: A new challenger has emerged in the world of gaming controllers, aiming to take on Sony's DualSense Edge. Nacon's Revolution 5 Unlimited controller is an officially licensed PlayStation 5 gamepad that also works seamlessly with PCs. This premium controller is packed with features that will delight competitive gamers, including a staggering number of customizable shortcut buttons and control profiles. The interactive control screen allows users to easily navigate through the plethora of options available, making it easier than ever to tailor their gaming experience. The Revolution 5 Unlimited is priced at $230, placing it firmly in the high-end category of gaming controllers. Its impressive specs include TMR (tunneling magnetoresistance) technology for its joysticks, which uses less power while reducing physical wear and tear. One notable design change on this controller is the asymmetric stick layout, swapping the traditional placement of the joystick and D-pad on the left side. This unconventional design may take some getting used to, but it offers a more comfortable gaming experience for those who adapt to it. The R5U also features trigger blockers, which can be toggled to reduce trigger travel. This is particularly useful in games that require quick actions, such as racing or fighting games. Additionally, there are four custom shortcut buttons below the trigger toggles and two more between the L and R trigger pairs. The Revolution 5 Unlimited's design may take some time to get accustomed to, especially for those familiar with traditional controller layouts. However, its innovative features and high-end specs make it an intriguing option for competitive gamers looking to upgrade their gaming experience. The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited controller offers a high level of customization that may be overwhelming for some users. The controller's D-pad can be swapped out for one with an 8-way layout, ideal for fighting game enthusiasts who need precise control over their characters' movements. In addition to the D-pad swap, the joystick heads are also interchangeable, providing three different profiles to suit various hand shapes and sizes. These profiles range from a concave shape that fits snugly in the palm to a high concave design for those with larger hands. The controller's weight can be customized as well, with adjustable weights ranging from 10 to 16 grams that can be embedded into each grip. This feature allows users to tailor the feel of the controller to their liking and may appeal to gamers who prefer a more substantial build in their hands. A dedicated charging dock is included with the R5U, which features a pogo pin connection for easy charging and a USB pass-through port that connects to both the console and wireless dongle. However, this controller lacks one feature found on some other gaming controllers: remote-start capabilities. The wireless connection requires a USB dongle that can be plugged into either the console or the companion dock, although it uses USB-A ports rather than the newer USB-C standard used by the PS5. This means users will need to use an additional cable if they want to connect their controller via wire. The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited (R5U) controller offers a range of customization options that can be accessed through its built-in screen or the companion mobile app. The app allows users to apply complex button setups and key bindings to the controller's numerous buttons, as well as display the pad's battery level and current connectivity status. In addition to these features, the R5U also includes a "Shooter Pro" mode that can be activated through the app. This mode removes the dead zone on the joystick, allowing for even more precise control when shooting. Users can adjust the dead zone or invert the joysticks in the companion app. The built-in screen of the R5U provides a convenient way to customize settings locally without needing to use the app. I found it useful to remap the shortcut buttons on the rear of the pad to avoid accidentally triggering them, and also mapped L3 and R3 inputs for quicker triggering. Users can switch between the controller's various modes, including PC mode, which offers 1000Hz polling rates on a wired connection and up to 500Hz wirelessly. The Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited controller offers an unprecedented level of customization through its companion app, available on both iOS and Android devices. This app allows users to fine-tune various aspects of their gaming experience, including response curves, audio equalizers, and even the RGB light ring's color scheme. However, it appears that this extensive customization capability comes with some trade-offs. The controller's interactive screen is not touch-sensitive, forcing users to navigate through menus using the D-pad instead. This design choice has a notable impact on compatibility, as certain PS5 games that rely heavily on touchpad controls are no longer accessible. One such game is Ghost of Yotei, which utilizes advanced touchpad motions beyond simple tapping as core gameplay mechanics. Reviewing the controller with this game was particularly frustrating due to its limited compatibility. Additionally, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited lacks another key feature found in some PS5 controllers: adaptive triggers. In comparison to other premium gaming pads on the market, the DualSense Edge from Sony stands out as a major competitor to the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited. With features like replaceable sticks, customizable button profiles, and adjustable stick sensitivity, it offers an impressive level of versatility that is unmatched by most other controllers. Ultimately, the Nacon Revolution 5 Unlimited's unique blend of customization options and PC compatibility makes it an attractive choice for gamers seeking a highly adaptable controller experience. articles.title: Vietnam's Trade Surplus with US Sparks Controversy
articles.summary: The controversy centers around allegations that Vietnam exploits loopholes to evade tariffs on its exports to the US.
articles.content: Vietnam's massive trade surplus with the US has sparked controversy in recent months, with some officials accusing the country of exploiting loopholes to evade tariffs. Former US Ambassador to Vietnam Marc Knapper disputes this claim, stating that only a small fraction of Vietnamese exports to the US are involved in illegal transshipment. This practice involves falsifying the country of origin to avoid paying tariffs on imported goods. According to Knapper, who served as ambassador from 2022 to 2026, such activities are not widespread and Vietnam has been actively working to curb them. Knapper made his comments at a recent conference in Ho Chi Minh City, where he explained that the term "transshipment has taken on different meanings depending on one's perspective. He emphasized that legitimate trade practices, including the assembly of goods from neighboring countries, should not be confused with illicit activities. The issue is significant because it could impact Vietnam's reputation as a reliable trading partner and potentially lead to tariffs being imposed on its exports. However, Knapper noted that his country has been making efforts to crack down on fraudulent transshipment practices, working closely with US Customs and Border Protection. As the debate over transshipment continues, some officials have raised concerns about the Trump administration's broad definition of the term, which could potentially label normal supply chain activities as illicit. The Trump administration has accused several countries of engaging in a Great Transshipment Scam that allegedly costs the US economy $19 billion to $26 billion annually in tariff revenue. This claim is part of a broader effort to restrict transshipment practices, which involve diverting parts of a Chinese supply chain overseas to take advantage of lower tariffs. A significant portion of Vietnam's massive $140 billion trade surplus with the US has been accumulated despite the imposition of tariffs by Washington on Vietnamese goods. According to Marc Knapper, a former ambassador, this surplus is not driven by illicit transshipment practices. Instead, American consumers and manufacturers have come to appreciate the quality and value of made in Vietnam products. The US has imposed various tariffs on Vietnamese goods, including a 12.5% duty on many items following an investigation into forced labor practices in the country. Vietnam initially agreed to accept a 20% tariff on its regular exports to the US under a trade agreement announced in July 2025. However, this deal also included provisions for a higher 40% tariff on goods deemed to have been transshipped from China. The US Supreme Court's decision in February has put the initial trade agreement in limbo by deeming most of President Trump's tariffs unlawful. This development adds complexity to the ongoing debate over transshipment practices and their impact on global trade dynamics. The trend of companies relocating parts of their supply chains out of China and into Southeast Asia is gaining momentum, driven by factors such as rising U.S. protectionism and increasing costs in China. This China plus one strategy allows companies to diversify their production bases and improve supply-chain resilience. Chinese businesses are also expanding into the region, not just for manufacturing but also as a new consumer market. In fact, they have coined the term chuhai" to describe this approach of doing business in Southeast Asia and Vietnam. This shift is being driven by companies seeking to tap into emerging markets and gain a competitive edge. Trade between China and ASEAN countries has reached historic highs, exceeding $1 trillion for the first time in 2025. This milestone underscores the growing importance of regional trade agreements and partnerships in the global economy. The development of Vietnam's infrastructure is also playing a key role in its emergence as a major trading hub. A planned railway linking Vietnam to China has received an additional $3.3 billion in funding from the National Assembly, with officials aiming for completion by 2030 despite some delays due to land clearance issues. articles.title: Federal Reserve Interest Rate Decisions Show Limited Impact on Analyst Forecasts
articles.summary: A study found that stock market analysts tend to be unresponsive when adjusting their forecasts after Fed meetings, with only about one in five companies' price targets revised by analysts.
articles.content: The US Federal Reserve's interest rate decisions have far-reaching consequences for consumers and businesses alike. When the Fed announces a change in its interest rate, people expect a ripple effect on borrowing costs and prices of goods such as housing and consumer products. However, new research suggests that stock market analysts tend to be unresponsive when it comes to adjusting their forecasts after Fed meetings. Despite numerous meetings between 2000 and 2020 where the Fed raised or lowered interest rates, a study found that only about one in five companies' price targets were revised by analysts working at investment houses and brokerages. The researchers from the University of Toronto's Rotman School of Management discovered that these targets lose accuracy after a Fed meeting. When interest rates rise, stock prices tend to fall, but analysts' forecasts often overestimate future prices. Conversely, when rates drop, stock prices increase, yet analysts underestimate their value. A closer look at the data reveals that the prediction inaccuracy is more pronounced during periods of rate hikes. The researchers found that forecast accuracy decreased by about 13% when interest rates were raised. In contrast, a larger decline of over 16% was observed when rates were lowered. The findings have significant implications for investors who rely on these forecasts to make informed decisions about buying or selling stocks. The study highlights the need for analysts to be more responsive and accurate in their price target revisions following Fed meetings. The study's findings suggest that analysts' mistakes are not uncommon, and can be attributed to various factors. According to lead author Junhao Liu, a senior accounting lecturer at the University of Melbourne, analysts often make errors due to either intentional or unintentional reasons. A closer examination of the data reveals that one primary cause of inaccuracy is analysts' failure to adjust the discount rate used in their forecasting models. This crucial component takes into account various factors such as risk, interest rates, and the cost of tying up capital over time, effectively converting a stock's future value into its present-day equivalent. The study indicates that companies with high exposure to interest rates, including financial institutions and highly leveraged firms, are more susceptible to forecast inaccuracy following Fed meetings. Conversely, investment houses with macroeconomists on staff tend to exhibit less pronounced inaccuracies when it comes to predicting the impact of interest rate changes. Notably, even top-performing analysts were unable to accurately adjust their forecasts after a Fed rate increase, which occurred 29 times during the studied period. However, these same analysts showed improved accuracy in forecasting around rate decreases, which happened 28 times. The study's authors suggest that sell-side analysts may not be interpreting macroeconomic information accurately when adjusting their stock forecasts after Federal Reserve meetings. A closer examination of these adjustments reveals a pattern where analysts tend to underreact to rate hikes and overreact to rate cuts. This is a concern because accurate forecasting is crucial for investors making informed decisions about their portfolios. The research implies that analysts may be hesitant to adjust their price targets due to various constraints, such as the potential impact on their reputations or the difficulty of accurately assessing the interest rate change's effects. Given the significant changes in monetary policy during and after the pandemic, these findings could provide valuable insights for investors seeking to navigate the market and for analysts striving to improve their forecasting accuracy amidst rapid shifts in interest rates. The study suggests that sell-side analysts tend to adjust their target-price forecasts inadequately after Federal Reserve meetings, indicating a potential disconnect between market expectations and actual monetary policy changes. This disparity could have significant implications for investors navigating the market, as it may lead to inaccurate price predictions and poor investment decisions. articles.title: Huge Fled US After FDA Pressure, Now at Center of Thailand Bodybuilder Deaths Investigation
articles.summary: A former model turned bodybuilder has been linked to several young men who have died under mysterious circumstances in Thailand.
articles.content: A former model turned bodybuilder has been at the center of a disturbing trend that has claimed the lives of several young men in Thailand. Huge, a 44-year-old entrepreneur, fled the United States after facing legal pressure from the Food and Drug Administration. He had built a reputation as an icon of the biohacking community with his motto a day natty is a day wasted. His followers were drawn to his unconventional lifestyle, which included a focus on physical appearance and self-optimization. Huge's influence extended beyond online communities, as some young men moved to Thailand to live with him. The documentary series Get Huge: Looksmaxxing to Death, set to premiere on Hulu in November, sheds light on the darker side of this subculture. The series focuses on Huge's role in the deaths of several individuals, including Laith Abdallah Algaz, a biohacker and penis enlargement influencer who died under mysterious circumstances. The investigation that follows is not your typical true-crime documentary. Instead, it delves into the world of self-optimization, where individuals engage in extreme practices such as injecting themselves with pig's brains and liquified gold. Alliances within this community are fleeting, and social media plays a significant role in promoting these activities. The series raises questions about the consequences of prioritizing physical appearance above all else. As Huge's influence continues to grow, concerns have been raised about the impact on his followers and the broader implications for society. As the documentary crew delved deeper into Huge's world, they began to notice a disturbing trend. The individuals surrounding him were dropping like flies, and it became clear that there was more to the story than initially met the eye. The filmmakers realized that what was being presented as a blueprint for success was actually a facade, hiding a darker reality. This realization led them to re-evaluate their approach to the documentary, focusing on the underlying issues rather than just Huge's persona. According to Lee, the problem lies in the fact that viewers can't distinguish between what's real and what's staged. The documentary is not just about Huge's rise to fame but also about the impact of the manosphere on young people who may be watching as a guide for their own lives. The filmmakers' interest in Huge's world was sparked by the growing influence of the manosphere, particularly the looksmaxxing movement popularized by influencers such as Clavicular and Androgenic. This online self-optimization culture is built around extreme and rigid views of masculinity, which can have serious consequences for those who subscribe to it. The documentary crew's fascination with this topic began long before Clav became a household name, with journalist and podcast producer Jennings Brown starting his investigation in 2023. The documentary crew's investigation into the death of Algaz led them to examine the world of looksmaxxing, where men obsess over physical appearance and often engage in extreme behaviors to achieve their goals. Their research revealed a disturbing pattern of deaths linked to this community, with two prominent members, Nick Weisser and Josh Brooks, dying under mysterious circumstances in 2018 and 2021 respectively. Thai police ultimately concluded that Algaz died from blunt force head trauma in January 2023, found deceased in Huge's home with his pants around his ankles. The men featured in the documentary "Get Huge often claim to value male friendship, but their relationships are marred by constant bickering and enabling behavior. This toxic dynamic is exploited for the sake of viewership, as they film themselves engaging in increasingly self-destructive activities. A former associate of Hughes, identified only as Elon Muscular, comments on the group's dynamics: They don't take care of each other. This sentiment is echoed by Lee, who notes that bodyhacking and looksmaxxing have a homoerotic aspect. He explains that many of the substances used in the community originated from gay culture. Hughes uses his entourage to reinforce his macho image, going so far as to tattoo his name on one member and pay for another's breast implants. In a disturbing scene, he administers drugs to some members of the group with the goal of increasing their sexual attraction to him. This raises uncomfortable questions about Hughes' motivations and ethics. The documentary crew captures these moments without judgment, leaving viewers to draw their own conclusions about Hughes' actions. Lee reflects on her experience filming Get Huge": "As a woman, it was incredibly challenging to witness" how Hughes treats his girlfriends. articles.summary: A team led by Sebastian Morris at the University of Cambridge has discovered a new type of turbulence that exists solely in the quantum realm.
articles.content: Researchers have made a groundbreaking observation of a previously unknown type of turbulence that exists solely in the quantum realm. Dubbed "ultraquantum" turbulence, this phenomenon is characterized by chaotic and irregular currents that deviate from classical fluid dynamics. In normal fluids, turbulence manifests as whirlpools or eddies, but in quantum fluids, it takes on a more exotic form. Ultraquantum turbulence may be representative of the behavior of various exotic systems, including liquid helium and neutron stars. These environments are governed by unique rules that differ significantly from those governing everyday fluids and gases. When perturbed, quantum fluids tend to remain still, but they develop intricate patterns of thin, string-like whirlpools before returning to equilibrium. To study ultraquantum turbulence, a team led by Sebastian Morris at the University of Cambridge used an innovative setup involving thousands of potassium atoms cooled to extremely low temperatures using lasers and electromagnetic fields. This allowed the researchers to create a dilute quantum gas that mimicked the behavior of a fluid in the quantum realm. The team then contained the atoms within a cylindrical shape, just a few dozen micrometres in size, to study their behavior under controlled conditions. The researchers then created a disturbance within the ultra-quantum fluid by controlling the interactions between its constituent atoms and their energies. This induced turbulence and vortices within the fluid, which was contained within a cylindrical shape just a few dozen micrometres in size. To study this phenomenon, Morris and his colleagues used a sheet of laser light to isolate and image just one slice of the cylinder at a time, rather than attempting to capture the entire structure. This approach allowed them to observe the intricate tangles and patterns that emerged within the fluid as it became more turbulent and disordered. The team obtained numerous images, which revealed the distribution of vortices as they formed, merged, or broke apart. They observed how these vortices connected into rings or migrated towards the edge of the cylinder, tracing the gradual decline in turbulence and disorder within the quantum fluid. Intriguingly, the researchers discovered that this process exhibited similarities with a previously studied quantum system: liquid helium. While helium is much denser than the ultra-quantum fluid, its atoms interact more strongly, yet the formation of order within both systems appears to follow a universal pattern. Researchers have long struggled to visualize vortices in ultraquantum fluids due to their complex nature and three-dimensional structure. However, a recent breakthrough has provided precise experimental evidence supporting mathematical models of this phenomenon. The new study's findings have been hailed as phenomenal by experts, with some even suggesting that future experiments could reveal more about the behavior of vortices if they image multiple slices of atoms simultaneously. This approach is indeed being explored by the research team behind the study. The universal pattern observed in both helium and ultraquantum fluid turbulence suggests that this phenomenon may be more widespread than previously thought, with potential implications for understanding similar processes in distant environments.
